What ECO CARE is

2

For pharmacies & healthcare providers

Counselling support, built from the Needs Analysis

①

Check before crushing or splitting

Confirm whether a score line is for dosing or just easier swallowing, and whether a modified-release or coated tablet is safe to crush at all — the single most-prioritised topic in both countries' surveys.

②

Time disposal guidance to the moment

Offer take-back guidance at therapy change, at treatment completion, and when a patient is clearing a deceased relative's medicines — the points the Needs Analysis found disposal advice is most needed and least often given.

③

Flag leftover antibiotics specifically

Part-used courses and children's antibiotic syrups are commonly kept "for next time." Remind patients to return them — antibiotic syrups also carry a short shelf life once opened.

3

For patients & caregivers

Five rules for medicines at home

Your pharmacist gave you this code because these are exactly the questions ECO CARE was built to answer. It doesn't replace their advice — it's the same advice, ready whenever you need to check it again.

01

Ask before crushing

Not every tablet can be split or crushed safely — check with your pharmacist first.

02

Measure liquid doses properly

Use the syringe or cup that came with the medicine, never a kitchen spoon.

03

Store it out of reach

Cool, dry, out of light, and out of reach of children — not the bathroom cabinet.

04

Finish or return antibiotics

Never save leftovers "just in case," and never share them with someone else.

05

Return, don't bin or flush

Unused or expired medicines go back to a pharmacy — never the bin, sink, or toilet.

Why it matters

Medicines that end up in water or soil affect wildlife too — not just people.

·

Frequently asked

Common questions

Can I crush my tablet to make it easier to swallow?

Sometimes — but not always. A score line can mean "split for dosing" or just "easier to swallow," and modified-release or coated tablets often must not be crushed at all. Ask your pharmacist before you do.

What do I do with leftover antibiotics?

Don't keep them for later and don't share them. Close the container and return it to any pharmacy — this is especially common with children's antibiotic syrups, which are rarely finished exactly to the last dose.

Why can't I just bin old medicines or flush them?

Medicines flushed or binned can end up in soil and waterways, where they affect wildlife and water quality. ECO CARE's own survey found that in both Slovenia and Croatia, this is still one of the most common disposal habits — pharmacy return is the safe alternative.

Where do I return unused or expired medicines?

In Slovenia, community pharmacies, collection centres, and mobile collection units all accept waste medicines. In Croatia, pharmacies collect them in sealed containers under the national take-back system — look for a drop-off container at the counter.

Is this the same as my doctor's or pharmacist's instructions?

It supports their advice, not replaces it. Your label and your pharmacist always take priority — ECO CARE fills in the everyday, practical detail there usually isn't time for at the counter.

Not a single stakeholder in either country said patients fully understand the environmental consequences of improper medicine disposal — the strongest single finding of the Needs Analysis, and the reason environmental impact is a core ECO CARE topic, not an add-on.
